about: Happy Then Shocked is a four-square layout: two stacked photos of the same young man on the right and two empty white boxes on the left for captions. In the top photo he is beaming with a wide toothy smile; in the bottom photo, taken a second later, the smile has dropped and his mouth hangs open in disbelief while his eyes stare at something off-screen. It captures the moment good news reveals its catch, the instant joy turns into realization.
origin: The two frames are stills of the same man reacting on camera, set beside an empty column in the style of the Drake format. Who the man is and which video the stills come from are not reliably known.
usage:
Write the good news in the top-left box, next to the smile, and the catch in the bottom-left box, next to the shocked face. Each box should be a short statement; the shift in expression delivers the punchline.

It is built for reversals: payday followed by rent, a free trial followed by the auto-renewal, an A on the test followed by finding out it was the practice test. The second line hits hardest when it is a logical consequence the person should have seen coming.
ideas: got an A on the exam
my team is up 3-0 at halftime
